what_happened: Re-measured the four remediation-target repos directly rather than trusting the dispatch's prose. Logos/Theory's 2026-11-07 by-hand repair (claimed to 'now match the canonical source exactly') is actually INCOMPLETE: it still carries (1) a wezterm-clear-status.sh orphan under UserPromptSubmit|* in CWD-relative form (script absent from current source entirely) and (2) a stale CWD-relative validate-no-task-references.sh duplicate registered under PostToolUse|Write|Edit, while the current, correct registration lives under PreToolUse|Write|Edit -- so the hook now runs TWICE per Write/Edit in that repo. The plan/implementation phase must re-verify Theory's post-sweep state rather than treating it as an already-clean control.

Found a defect shape not named by this task's SUB-BEHAVIOR section or by sibling task 527's (a)/(b)/(c) taxonomy: a hook registration surviving under a DIFFERENT EVENT than the one current source declares it under (not just a different matcher within the same event). Logos/Theory's PostToolUse|Write|Edit carries a stale validate-no-task-references.sh copy while current source registers that same hook only under PreToolUse|Write|Edit. merge_hook_event_array/hook_identity operate per-event-key (deep_merge calls them once per top-level hooks.<EVENT> array independently), so an identity match across a changed matcher within one event is already handled by the dispatch's SUB-BEHAVIOR note, but an identity match across a changed EVENT is not -- the two blocks live in entirely separate top-level arrays and are never compared to each other by any existing or dispatch-described mechanism. Flagging this as an open design question for the plan: does 'the source is authoritative about WHERE its own hooks register' extend to event, not just matcher?

Confirmed the dispatch's first LIVE INSTANCE (claude-ready-signal.sh orphan) is far more widespread than the single host-repo citation suggests: this exact host repo's own deployed .claude/settings.json still carries it unfixed today (bash scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh, bare CWD-relative, no .claude/ or ~/ anchor at all), AND ModelBuilder, Logos/Website, and Logos/Theory all carry a second variant (bash ~/.config/nvim/scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh, ~/-anchored). The ~/-anchored variant is identity-INELIGIBLE under both merge.lua's hook_identity() and the lint's D1/D2 carve-out (externally-provided, never fragment-coverage-checked), so it must NOT be swept even though no current source surface declares it -- a concrete worked example for the plan's 'custom-hook carve-out must survive' acceptance criterion, found via direct repo inspection rather than constructed as a hypothetical.

Plan-phase re-verification of all five named deploys via a jq census confirmed the research report's field table exactly: host repo still carries the CWD-relative 'bash scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh' orphan (28 regs), ModelBuilder and Logos/Website each carry the idle_prompt-widened Notification block plus Stop|* tts-notify/wezterm-notify pair (12 regs each), Logos/Theory is incompletely repaired (30 regs; stale PostToolUse|Write|Edit validate-no-task-references.sh plus wezterm-clear-status.sh), theorem_proving_in_lean4 carries dead-script registrations (13 regs). No research claim needed correction.

The extension repo registry (~/.local/share/nvim/neotex-ai/extension-repo-registry.json) is unusable as the deploy-enumeration source for the before/after measurement: it holds 313 entries of which 311 are /tmp test fixtures and only 2 are real repos, while a filesystem scan finds 14 repos with .claude-extensions.json and ~34 directories with a deployed .claude/ tree. The plan therefore specifies filesystem enumeration, not the registry, as the control-set source.
